 Harris County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0027
 Jennifer Watts, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Jennifer Watts
Date:
May 15, 2025
Location:
Offices of Marshall & Dominguez LLP
Examining attorney:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Kyle Sanders, Marshall & Dominguez LLP
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record here, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this matter.
Q: Fair enough. Let's talk about the accident. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was in Houston, Texas, at an intersection, making a left turn across the opposing lanes.
Q: What were you driving?
A: A sedan. It was my own vehicle, which I had been driving for a few years.
Q: Describe what happened as you began your turn.
A: I had a green light, but I was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. When I saw one, I started moving. Then a vehicle coming
from the other direction struck the front driver's side of my car.
Q: Did you see that vehicle before the impact?
A: Only for a moment. I remember it was closer than I expected, and I had no time to react.
Q: Did you feel anything at the moment of impact?
A: My body was thrown against the seatbelt and then toward the door. My left shoulder hit the frame of the window hard.
Q: When did you first notice pain in your shoulder?
A: Almost immediately, but I assumed it was bruising. Over the next day it became much worse and I could barely lift my arm.
Q: Did you seek medical treatment?
A: Yes. I went to an emergency department that evening, and I was later referred to an orthopedic doctor.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've had physical therapy several times a week, a series of injections, and I've been using a sling for part of the time. The
doctor has discussed possible further evaluation, but I haven't decided on that yet.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are hard. I have trouble dressing, reaching for items on high shelves, and sleeping on my left side. I had to stop a
hobby I enjoyed, woodworking, because I can't hold tools steady.
Q: Have you been able to work since the accident?
A: I've been working, but with restrictions. I asked my supervisor to move me to tasks that don't require lifitng with my left arm,
and I've had to leave early on some days for appointments.
Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior problems with that shoulder?
A: No, not that I can recall. I had no treatment for it before.
Q: Thank you. We'll take a short break.
</page>
